lines.trans: Two mint teas and three lemon tarts for table four under the tree!
Coming right up! Ziad, take the hot teapot to the corner window table!
Table two says this almond crust is the best pastry on Jasmine Street!
Tell table two the secret was my two kitchen apprentices on Wednesday!
How many slices of lemon tart are left on tray four, Salma?
Count them: one, two, three—out of forty slices in fifteen minutes!
Good thing you baked two extra trays of warm cinnamon rolls just in case!
Listen—the room just went quiet! Someone is tapping a music stand!
Our neighbour from number ten brought his violin case inside Room Nine!
Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you—come listen at the door!
Save those last three slices of tart for Suad, Tariq, and Mazen!
Aprons off—it is six o'clock on Friday!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Arabic noun meaning 'origin', used in من أصل to express 'out of a total'.

examples.text: نجحت بتسع مواد من أصل عشرة هالفصل.
examples.trans: I passed nine courses out of a total of ten this semester.

examples.text: عيلتنا أصلها من السلط بس ساكنين بعمان.
examples.trans: Our family originally comes from Salt, though we live in Amman.

meanings.note: Literally 'tastiest', the top Levantine Arabic compliment for food.

examples.text: هادي أطيب منسف أكلتها بحياتي، يسلمو إيديك!
examples.trans: This is the most delicious mansaf I've ever eaten in my life—bless your hands!

examples.text: قهوة الهيل الصبح أطيب إشي بالدنيا.
examples.trans: Cardamom coffee in the morning is the best thing in the world.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: An imperative-only word: تعال to a man, تعالي to a woman, تعالوا to a group. Other tenses use إجا.

examples.trans: Come and sit next to me.
Come to the kitchen, all of you!

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Polite everyday reply meaning 'yes / at your service / right away'.

examples.text: حاضر يا ستي، دقيقتين وبجيبلك كاسة المي.
examples.trans: Right away, ma'am—two minutes and I'll bring you a glass of water.

examples.text: لا تشيل هم، حاضر، بمر عالبنك عنك.
examples.trans: Don't worry—consider it done, I'll stop by the bank for you.

meanings.note: From ح-م-ل ('to carry, hold'); names a music stand (حامل النوتة) or lamp/book holder.

examples.text: حطينا الورقة على حامل النوتة الخشب.
examples.trans: We set the sheet on the wooden music stand.

examples.text: حامل المفاتيح معلق ورا مكتب الاستقبال.
examples.trans: The key rack hangs behind the reception desk.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Common Arabic verb meaning 'to knock' or 'tap'.

examples.text: في حدا عم بدقّ عالباب، شوف مين اجا.
examples.trans: Someone is knocking on the door—go see who came.

examples.text: دقّيتلك مرتين مبارح بس تلفونك كان مسكّر.
examples.trans: I called you twice yesterday, but your phone was off.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Male given name, here referring to Rami's older brother.

examples.text: زياد بيساعد أخوه الصغير بحسابات المقهى.
examples.trans: Ziad helps his younger brother with the café's accounts.

examples.text: اسأل زياد وين حط الفواتير الشهرية.
examples.trans: Ask Ziad where he put the monthly invoices.

meanings.note: Placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'extra' (قطع زيادة extra pieces, الدرج الزيادة the extra stairs).

examples.trans: I brought two extra chairs for the courtyard.
I put a little extra mint in the tea.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسرار.

examples.trans: Rest assured, your secret is safe with us.

examples.text: سر الكيكة الزاكية هو الليمون الطازج.
examples.trans: The secret to tasty cake is fresh lemon.

meanings.note: Female given name of the retired piano teacher.

examples.text: المس سعاد بتعلمنا العزف على البيانو من خمس سنين.
examples.trans: Ms. Suad has been teaching us to play piano for five years.

examples.text: خالتو سعاد دايماً بتجيب حلويات معها بس تزورنا.
examples.trans: Auntie Suad always brings sweets with her when she visits us.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Female given name belonging to the café's morning baker.

examples.text: سلمى بتخبز الكرواسون والخبز كل يوم الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma bakes the croissants and bread every day at dawn.

examples.text: سلمى جابت صينية كعك طازة للضيوف.
examples.trans: Salma brought a tray of fresh cookies for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

شال.gloss: to carry away; remove; lift out

meanings.en: to carry away; remove; lift out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشيل, بيشيل).

examples.text: بنقدر نشيل أربع صناديق بخمس دقايق.
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes.
Sparkling water lifts the stain right out.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of ضل ('to remain'); standard Jordanian for 'there is ... left'.

examples.trans: He has two valves left on the shelf.
How much time is left until noon?

meanings.note: Male given name of the veteran handyman.

examples.text: المعلم طارق صلّح الحنفية والمفصلات بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: Master Tariq fixed the faucet and the hinges in half an hour.

examples.text: اسأل عمي طارق إذا معه المفك الكبير.
examples.trans: Ask Uncle Tariq if he has the big screwdriver with him.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Plural command form from عدّ ('to count') with the 'them' ending.

examples.text: عدّوا الكراسي منيح قبل ما يبلش الحفل.
examples.trans: Count the chairs carefully before the event begins.

examples.text: عدّيت المصاري مرتين عشان أتأكد من الحساب.
examples.trans: I counted the money twice to make sure of the total.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: The warm scent of cinnamon filled the kitchen.
We ate a cinnamon roll with tea.

meanings.note: Singulative of collective قشر ('peel, bark, shell'); قشرة الليمونة means 'the skin/zest of the lemon'.

examples.text: قشرة الليمون الأصفر ريحتها قوية وحلوة.
examples.trans: Yellow lemon peel has a strong, sweet scent.

examples.text: بتحط سلمى برش قشرة ليمون بعجينة الكيك.
examples.trans: Salma puts grated lemon peel into the cake batter.

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: In questions كم + singular noun asks 'how many?'; in statements كم + singular noun means 'a few' (كم دقيقة 'a few minutes').

examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Rami.

examples.text: كم لفة قرفة بيقدر فرنك يخبز؟
examples.trans: How many cinnamon rolls can your oven bake?

meanings.note: In Levantine Arabic, a noun for the violin (also pronounced كمنجة).

examples.text: صوت الكمنجة مع البيانو طلع كتير حنون ورايق.
examples.trans: The sound of the violin with the piano came out super tender and mellow.

examples.text: بنت خالتي بتتعلم عزف الكمنجة بالمعهد الموسيقي.
examples.trans: My cousin is learning to play the violin at the music conservatory.

meanings.note: Plural of لفافة ('roll/scroll'), used in bakeries for cinnamon rolls.

examples.text: عملت سلمى لفائف قرفة سخنة مع سكر ناعم عالوجه.
examples.trans: Salma made warm cinnamon rolls with powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: لقينا لفافة ورق قديمة مربوطة بخيط جوا الصندوق.
examples.trans: We found an old paper scroll tied with string inside the box.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Male given name of the guesthouse owner.

examples.text: مازن استقبل النزلاء بنفسه وساعدهم بالشنط.
examples.trans: Mazen greeted the guests himself and helped them with their bags.

examples.text: اتصل بمازن قبل ما نطبع المنيو الجديد.
examples.trans: Call Mazen before we print the new menu.

meanings.note: Plural of متدرّب (trainee/apprentice), from تدرّب (to train).

examples.text: في متدرّب جديد عم بتعلم شغل الحلويات مع سلمى.
examples.trans: There's a new apprentice learning pastry work with Salma.
The trainees at the company helped set up the exhibition.

meanings.note: Masculine Levantine noun (plural مراييل) worn while cooking, painting, or crafting.

examples.text: البس مريول الرسم قبل ما تفتح الألوان.
examples.trans: Put on the painting apron before you open the paints.
The apron got splashed all over with blue ink.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic bakery noun for pastries and baked doughs.

examples.text: جبنا صحن معجنات مشكلة بالجبنة والزعتر للفطور.
examples.trans: We brought a platter of assorted cheese and za'atar pastries for breakfast.

examples.text: المخبز هاد مشهور بالمعجنات الطازة كل يوم الصبح.
examples.trans: This bakery is famous for its fresh pastries every morning.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: A very common herb used in Levantine tea and cuisine.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Feminine past tense of هدي ('to calm down/go quiet'), agreeing with الغرفة.

examples.text: أخيراً هدي الشارع بالليل بعد ما روّحوا الناس.
examples.trans: The street finally quieted down at night after people went home.

examples.text: الغرفة هديت فجأة أول ما بلشت سعاد تعزف.
examples.trans: The room suddenly went quiet as soon as Suad started playing.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
